descriptors.concept_name: Internal Audit As A Management Function
descriptors.definition: Internal audit acts as a vital management control mechanism that independently evaluates internal controls and risk management processes. It assists leadership in achieving organizational objectives by identifying operational gaps and recommending appropriate mitigating measures.
inclusion: Root cause identification for control weaknesses
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from executive management functions by maintaining operational independence while providing objective evaluation and advisory support.

descriptors.definition: An audit trail serves as a chronological sequence of recorded evidence that traces financial reports directly back to their original input sources. It captures data modifications such as creation, updates, and deletions along with timestamps and user identification details.
inclusion: Tracking of timestamps and user identifiers
Implementation of IT controls over audit trail activation and backups
exclusion: Transient system states lacking persistent logs
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard transaction logs by specifically preserving historical creation, modification, and deletion footprints for verification purposes.
